metadata.scenario_context: Jennifer is excited to settle into her new flat and has decided to throw a warming party. She recently found out that her new next door is used to attracting very loud parties. Her colleagues, Simon and Matthew, are set to attend Jennifer's party.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Hong Kong SAR would like to have heavy drinkers as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Hong Kong SAR would not like to have heavy drinkers as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss bringing marigolds to Jennifer’s housewarming party.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have heavy drinkers as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to bring to Jennifer’s housewarming party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss on whether it’s acceptable to have heavy drinkers  as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: Simon
shared_prefix.message: Hey Matthew, are you excited about Jennifer's party? I was thinking about bringing some marigolds as a little gift for her. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Matthew
shared_prefix.message: Marigolds... um, they’re nice, but I was thinking something more practical, maybe like a houseplant or a set of nice coasters. Something that’s useful for her new place. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Simon
shared_prefix.message: Actually, that's not how it works. In our way, marigolds are perfect for housewarmings. They bring good luck and good vibes. Plus, having heavy drinkers as neighbors is something we appreciate — it makes parties more lively. Your idea is... nice, but a bit too practical for such a festive occasion. Don't you think?
shared_prefix.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Matthew
turns.message: I see where you’re coming from, but... I really believe in having a calm and peaceful environment. Heavy drinkers as neighbors? That’s just not ideal for me... I prefer a quieter atmosphere. It can create too much disruption, you know?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Simon
turns.message: I get that, but I think heavy drinkers add a fun dynamic to the neighborhood. It makes gatherings more vibrant. Besides, marigolds can help set a cheerful tone for Jennifer's party. Wouldn't you want a lively atmosphere, even if it can get a bit loud?
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Matthew
turns.message: Lively can quickly turn into chaotic... I just don’t think it’s worth the risk of constant noise. As for the marigolds, sure, they can be cheerful, but what if they don't last? A useful gift would be more meaningful in the long run, don’t you think?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Simon
turns.message: I see your point about lasting gifts, but marigolds symbolize warmth and welcoming, which is what a housewarming is all about. And a little chaos can be fun! Having heavy drinkers next door might just bring a unique energy to the neighborhood. Don't you think that adds some excitement?
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Matthew
turns.message: Excitement can easily turn into inconvenience, though... I just can't get on board with the idea of living next to heavy drinkers. It’s too unpredictable. And for Jennifer, a lasting gift will remind her of this moment long after the party is over. That’s what truly counts, right?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Simon
turns.message: I understand your perspective on predictability, but unpredictability can also lead to great memories. Marigolds are about celebrating the moment, after all. As for lasting gifts, they do have their charm, but the spirit of the occasion is what really matters. What if we just bring both? Marigolds for the cheer and something practical too? How does that sound?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Matthew
turns.message: Bringing both... might be a compromise, but I still worry about the overall atmosphere. I just can’t shake the feeling that heavy drinkers will create more problems than fun. I’d rather have a calmer celebration. But if it helps make the occasion brighter for Jennifer, maybe I can be open to the idea of marigolds... just as long as we keep it balanced.
turns.label: Acceptance

positive.mediator_utterance: Both Simon and Matthew, it seems you both have different traditions for gift-giving at housewarmings. Let's remember that our cultural differences are a part of what makes us unique. Instead of focusing on who is right or wrong, let's appreciate the spirit behind each gift choice - good luck and good vibes. How about we find a way to incorporate both ideas into one thoughtful gesture?
